key_insight: Charge-transfer-informed machine learning identifies promising boride substrates with tunable borophene binding, with Al- and Ag-based borides emerging as leading candidates.
engineering_relevance: Better substrate selection could ease borophene release and support its integration into quantum and energy technologies.
method: Combine DFT and ML to screen 1,356 boride surfaces for two borophene phases, ν1/6 and ν1/9.
Use ML-predicted charge transfer as an input to binding-energy prediction.
Apply SHAP analysis to identify influential descriptors, highlighting delocalized-electron properties.
evidence_signal: The screening identified 65 promising surfaces for ν1/6 and 73 for ν1/9, with additional DFT calculations on four representative cases used to validate ML predictions.
watch_item: The candidates remain computational predictions; experimental synthesis and successful borophene release are not demonstrated in the abstract.
paper_title: Machine Learning Aided Computational Discovery of Boride Substrates for Borophene Synthesis
